function.name: read_file
function.description: Returns one page of one existing file as JSON. The page starts at line `offset` (1-based), `column` bytes into that line, and holds up to `limit` lines; a long line continues on the next page. The file's text is in `content` (null for bytes that are not text, with their count in `binary`; a smaller `limit` may isolate them). To continue, call again with `next.line` as `offset` and `next.column` as `column`; `eof` is true at the end of the file, and `changed` is true when the file changed since your last page of it, so read it again from the start. One file per call. No globs, no directories, no recursion. May be refused.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to read.

column.description: Byte offset into the first line, from a previous page's next.column. Default 0.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Replaces the entire contents of path with content. This is not an edit, patch, or append — whatever was there is gone. Read the file before replacing it, every page until `eof` is true if you need all of its contents. Returns one of: applied; not written — nothing was written because the file exists and you have not read it, or it changed since you read it: read it, then write again; or outcome unknown — the write may have happened: do not retry it. The call's arguments, as JSON with `content` escaped, may be at most 61440 bytes; a longer call is refused whole and nothing is written.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to replace.

content.description: The complete new contents of the file.
